newsitem.title: ITALY: Jerry Hall takes early turn down Milan catwalk.
newsitem.headline: Jerry Hall takes early turn down Milan catwalk.

text.p: Texan model Jerry Hall, a blonde cascade of hair over one shoulder, took a turn along the catwalk for Iceberg at the Milan fashion shows on Saturday and fashion house Moschino blossomed with floral romance.

Hall, who is married to Rolling Stones rock star Mick Jagger, wore a white trousersuit to open Iceberg's spring/summer show before taking a seat in the audience to watch a procession of its 1997 ready-to-wear collection.
Iceberg skirts and pedal-pushers featured in eye-catching lime green and navy combinations and matched with pinstripes, followed by white with poppy red print on blouses and dresses.
Skirts fell to just below the knee while column dresses with cut-away shoulders and narrow round necks dropped straight to the ankle or were sometimes drawn in by a tiny belt at the hip.

Trousers were cut with a slight flare to the ankle and Iceberg also produced pink satiny skirts and trousersuits, sparkling sequinned tops in orange and bronze designed in a neat narrow rectangle across the breast and strapped behind.

In a leafy setting of trees and luxuriant plants inside the fair, Moschino sent models circulating around a fountain set in the runway in spectacular dresses made of sprays of roses, in one case topped by a huge cellophane wrap like a bouquet.
Other eccentric outfits included a dress decorated with an oriental woman's pale face and black hair in sequinned panels and a black dress hung with huge, tinkling golden hoops.

East met West and romance bloomed in the collection of mixed cultural influences from silver and gold decorated Indian silks, Chinese and Japanese effects like dresses hung with chopsticks, Wild West cowboy hats and demure summer gloves and cloche hats.
Bridget Cosgrave, a buyer from London's exclusive Harvey Nicholls store, said after the line-up, "It was fabulous and Moschino is always a very upbeat show.

"There are always a lot of elements that are just for fun and not for sale, playing on that Moschino frivolity. But when you strip it down and analyse it there are actually some very beautiful pieces in there," she said.
Indian-style shoulder sashes, tight-hipped toreador black pants with a neat cummerbund and Japanese style flower prints on pale backgrounds numbered among the diverse effects.

For evening Moschino paraded a wide range of black gowns, including a high-waisted design with a straight skirt which was reminiscent of a character from novel by early 19th century British novelist Jane Austen.

One full-length, off the shoulder number with a high waist and abundant soft pleats looked like it had just stepped off a Grecian urn while another was a 1920s style gown with long dripping fringes and matching fringed gloves to the elbow.

Italian designer Gianni Versace holds a series of shows for his main collection for the season later on Saturday, with Liam Gallagher, the lead singer of British pop group Oasis, expected to attend the latest with his actress girlfriend Patsy Kensit.
The shows end on Sunday with Italian designer Giorgio Armani presenting his main collection at the close of the day.
